subject: Regional data fencing & retention mechanics for hosted API
messages:

Subject: Regional data fencing / retention questions for hosted API

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking our questionnaire. A few focused questions from our compliance team so we can confirm whether hosted API meets our data residency and retention controls: 

1) Can you confirm where request payloads and generated outputs are stored by default (region/countries)?
2) What is the default retention window for request logs, usage telemetry, and model input/outputs? Can customers shorten this?
3) How are ephemeral caches (prefix/KV caches) handled — are they persisted to disk or only in-memory?
4) If Stratus requests a tenant-wide purge, what is the timeline and what artifacts do you provide as evidence?
5) Are backups or snapshots of tenant data geo-replicated outside the selected region?

Attached is our security assessment template; would appreciate short answers we can slot in.

Best,

Stratus Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Fiona Lewis <fiona.lewis@stratushealth.com>
Cc: security@stratushealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Regional data fencing / retention questions for hosted API

Hi Fiona — thanks for the clear list. Answers below are for our Hosted API product (default behavior) and notes on options for stricter controls. I pasted concise bullets so you can copy into your template; happy to expand any item.

1) Where stored by default
- Tenant request payloads and generated outputs are stored in the cloud region selected at account creation. For US customers we default to us-west-2; EU customers are routed to eu-west-1. We do not move tenant data outside the configured region for standard hosted accounts.

2) Default retention windows
- Request logs (structured access logs): 90 days by default.
- Usage telemetry (metrics/aggregates): 365 days (aggregated, not request-level).
- Model input/outputs (raw request/response bodies): 30 days by default.
- Customers can request custom TTLs at provisioning time; shorter TTLs (e.g., 7/14/30 days) are supported via account settings and enforced at the routing/storage layer.

3) Ephemeral caches
- Prefix/KV cache used for latency improvements is kept in-memory on serving nodes and backed by an in-region ephemeral cache tier. Cache entries are not written to durable storage by default. In the event of node replacement, cache is rebuilt from upstream requests.

4) Tenant-wide purge procedure
- Initiation: customer requests purge via Console or Support ticket (we recommend an authenticated request from an admin).
- Timeline: typical completion for hosted accounts is 24-72 hours for logical deletion of raw request/response bodies and 7-14 days to clear all cached traces and audit-indexed references.
- Evidence: we provide an attestation document (redwood_data_deletion_attestation_draft.pdf) and a deletion log export with timestamps and job ids. For regulated customers we can provide a signed deletion certificate and a timeline report.

5) Backups / geo-replication
- Backups are stored encrypted and kept within the selected region by default. We do not geo-replicate backups across continents for standard hosted accounts.

Additional notes
- Encryption: all data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed KMS integration available for enterprise plans.
- Audit logs: API-level audit logs are retained by default in-region and can be exported as part of the purge evidence set.
- SOC2 / compliance: we maintain SOC2 Type II and can provide the relevant artifact upon NDA.

Attaching a high-level data flow diagram and a draft deletion attestation; please tell me if you'd like tighter SLAs or a dedicated (reserved) deployment — that gives stronger isolation and faster purge guarantees.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Hi Fiona — thanks for the thoughtful questions and Mateo for the answers. Quick clarifications for Stratus: 

- Irrecoverability SLA: for standard Hosted API accounts we provide a contractual statement that logical deletion completes within 72 hours and that physical removal from backups will be completed within 30 days. For customers requiring a formal irrecoverability guarantee (shorter window and in-region-only backups), we recommend Redwood Dedicated or a Private deployment; those plans include a 7-day physical deletion SLA and can be scoped to not geo-replicate backups.

- KMS and transient plaintext: when customer-managed KMS is enabled, plaintext is not stored on disk in decrypted form. Transient in-memory decryption occurs for active request processing on serving nodes; these processes are ephemeral and memory is zeroed on job completion. We do not log plaintext request/response bodies when CMK is active; logs contain only metadata and encrypted references.

Next steps
- I can add the deletion SLA clause to the workbook and provide a signed Deletion Attestation after purge completion. If Stratus needs the 7-day physical deletion guarantee, I can open a Dedicated proposal and include a timeline and pricing addendum.

If that covers it, I'll send the finalized text for procurement.

Regards,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
